newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reinsurance buyers benefit from soft market.
newsitem.headline: Reinsurance buyers benefit from soft market.

text.p: Insurers looking to renew contracts or buy reinsurance for 1997 are generally finding cheaper deals as negotiations on price begin in earnest at the annual reinsurance gathering in this southern German resort.

After several almost disaster-free years and with new capacity entering the reinsurance market, industry sources said that, as expected, rates for some classes of business have fallen by as much as 30 percent.
Catastrophe reinsurers face the greatest pressure to reduce rates after three of the best years on record and no major insured disasters since 1992, one Lloyd's of London underwriter told Reuters.
Marine and aviation rates have also come under considerable cyclical pressure, with the advantage lying firmly with buyers of reinsurance at the Baden-Baden meeting which continues until Friday.

However, some business was still being largely rated on experience and loss statistics and shrugging off the worst of the cyclical pressures, reinsurers said, while liability reinsurance rates in particular were holding up well.
Reinsurers said this reflected the difficulty in quantifying the risks involved in liability cover, where large claims can emerge years in the future, as was the case with asbestosis.
By comparison, risks such as industrial fire can be estimated exactly and rates are more easily influenced by the availability of reinsurance capacity .

However, price was not the only concern of some insurers seeking to renew cover at Baden-Baden. Some acknowledged that prior to the last three years, reinsurers experienced one of the worst ever periods for the industry.
The late 1980s and early 1990s were littered with massive insured losses including hurricanes Andrew and Hugo, European windstorms and industrial disasters such as Exxon Valdez and Piper Alpha.

"As a reinsurance buyer I could put much more pressure on reinsurers to reduce rates...but we need the assistance of reinsurers," said one representative of a German insurer, adding that long term relationships were very important.
"Reinsurers need to build up some financial stability to cover us when needed. Good times for reinsurers means good times for reinsurance buyers too," he said.
